title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Prompt Sets, Model Onboarding, Quantization Profiles & Regression Triage Playbook (2026)
author: Priya Malhotra
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standardized approach for applied ML evaluations: the eval harness, prompt-set curation and benchmarking, model onboarding checklists, automated and manual quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and a regression triage process. The goal is to ensure consistent, reproducible, and scalable evaluation workflows that protect production quality while enabling efficient model rollouts.

Scope

- Applicable to all model onboarding and rollout activities for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Intended for ML engineers, evaluation engineers, product owners, and SREs involved in model validation and production monitoring.

Key Outcomes

- Repeatable eval runs with deterministic prompts and scoring.
- Prompt set coverage that reflects real product inputs and edge cases.
- Quantization profiles with documented accuracy/perf tradeoffs.
- Clear ownership and SLAs for regression detection and mitigation.

Roles & Ownership

- Applied ML / Eval Owner: owns harness configuration, prompt sets, and evaluation schedules.
- Model Owner: responsible for onboarding artifacts, retraining, and addressing flagged regressions.
- Platform/Runtime Owner (serving-runtime): provides perf/latency budgets and helps reproduce infra-related regressions.
- QA/PM: approves production acceptance criteria and representative prompt coverage.

Eval Harness Overview

- Infrastructure: eval-harness runs on a dedicated CI pool (project: eval-runner) and can target both CPU/GPU variants. Runs are triggered manually for onboarding and scheduled nightly for critical models.
- Data & Artifacts: all prompt sets, ground truth, and scoring configs are version-controlled in the eval repo (git tags match model-version tags).
- Determinism: random seeds, tokenization configs, and sampling parameters are fixed in the harness config to ensure reproducible comparisons.

Prompt Sets & Benchmarking Guidelines

Principles

1. Coverage-first: capture functional categories (intent, entity extraction, summarization), difficulty tiers (trivial, moderate, adversarial), and distributional examples from production telemetry.
2. Representative: prefer production-derived anonymized prompts where privacy allows.
3. Versioned & Reviewed: every prompt set is peer-reviewed and has a changelog entry.

Prompt Set Structure (recommended)

- Metadata: name, description, owner, created_at, labels, intended-use.
- Example rows: input_text, expected_output (or rubric), difficulty, tags, source_id.

Example prompt-set header (YAML)

```yaml
name: "conversational-faq-v1"
description: "Representative user questions for FAQ assistant."
owner: "applied-ml-team"
created_at: "2025-10-12"
labels: ["faq", "conversational", "prod-derived"]
```

Benchmarking Process

1. Select prompt set(s) and baseline model(s).
2. Define metrics: accuracy, ROUGE/L, BLEU (if applicable), factuality score, hallucination rate, latency P50/P95, and token cost.
3. Run harness with fixed seeds and collect raw outputs + per-sample logs.
4. Scoring: apply automated scorers and a human review sample (see QA thresholds below).
5. Generate report: include metric deltas vs baseline, per-category breakdowns, and failure clusters.

Quality Guardrails (Acceptance Criteria)

Automated thresholds (example):

- Accuracy >= 92% (core intents)
- Factuality precision >= 95% on knowledge-retrieval prompts
- Hallucination rate <= 1.5% on generation prompts
- Latency P95 <= 750ms on dedicated GPU pool (as measured by harness)

Human review gates:

- If automated metric delta > 2% negative vs baseline, run 200-sample human review.
- If >5% of samples are labeled as incorrect or harmful, block rollout and start regression triage.

Model Onboarding Checklist

Before canary/production rollout: (model owner completes and checks off)

1. Model artifact uploaded and verified (checksum + model-card).
2. Eval harness run vs current production baseline (report attached).
3. Prompt sets: run full suite (smoke + core + adversarial).
4. Quantization sweep (if applicable) with recommended profile documented.
5. Canary plan: traffic split, monitoring metrics, rollback criteria.
6. Cost/throughput analysis: token cost delta and expected throughput.
7. Security review (if model accesses private data or connectors).

Quantization Profiles & Best Practices

- Purpose: reduce memory and inference cost while bounding quality regressions.
- Profiles include target dtype (e.g., fp16, int8), per-layer calibration method, and expected throughput uplift.
- Sweep methodology:
  1. Start with fp16 baseline, measure metrics and perf.
  2. Apply per-layer asymmetric int8 with per-channel scaling.
  3. Re-run full eval suite and sample human checks.
  4. Document any tokens/queries where behavior diverges.

Quantization example metadata (CSV)

profile_name, dtype, calibration_method, expected_token_speedup, notes
int8-default,int8,kl_divergence,1.8x,"Good for majority of use-cases; higher hallucination risk on long-context generation"
fp16-safe,fp16,n/a,1.2x,"Default recommended for safety-first deployments"

Regression Triage Playbook

Trigger conditions (examples)

- Nightly eval detects metric regression > configured delta (default 2%).
- Customer-reported quality regression with reproducible example.
- Canary monitoring shows increased error rate or user-visible failures.

Initial Triage (first 60 minutes)

1. Triage owner (on-call applied-ml engineer) acknowledges and collects: failing sample IDs, eval run IDs, model versions, infra/serving variant.
2. Reproduce locally in harness using the same model artifact and runtime flags.
3. Classify regression: dataset shift, model quality regression, quantization/inference artifact, or infra-related (latency/timeouts).
4. If infra-related, escalate to runtime/sre team immediately; tag incident with relevant logs.

Investigation (4-48 hours)

- If model quality regression: run counterfactuals (compare logits, token probabilities), cluster failures by prompt tags, and run small-batch human eval on top-k failure clusters.
- If quantization regression: compare outputs between fp16/float baseline and quantized variant; consider per-layer re-calibration or roll back to safer profile.
- If data/regression induced by prompt drift: verify distribution against production telemetry and consider prompt-set augmentation.

Mitigation and Rollback

- Temporary mitigations: route traffic to fallback model variant, increase conservative decoding params (temperature/beam size), or enable cached responses for known-good queries.
- Permanent fixes: retrain/finetune with curated failure set, update quantization profile, or adjust model selection policy.
- Postmortem: every regression that triggers a blocked rollout requires a doc with root cause, mitigation, timeline, and owners. Add to the regression backlog for preventative work.

SLOs & Monitoring Signals

Primary evaluation SLOs (applied-ml):

- Nightly eval completeness: 100% of scheduled eval runs complete within 2 hours.
- Regression detection latency: median time from alert to triage start <= 45 minutes.
- False positive rate (auto-blocks): < 3% (requires human verification).

Monitoring signals to surface in dashboards:

- Per-model metric time series (accuracy, hallucination, factuality).
- Canary traffic error rates and latency percentiles.
- Per-prompt-tag failure rates and token cost deltas.

Runbook snippets & CLI

- Run a single eval locally (example):

```bash
# run eval harness for conversational-faq-v1 against model v1.3.0
./bin/eval-runner --model-path s3://models/redwood/v1.3.0 --prompt-set prompt-sets/conversational-faq-v1.json --outdir /tmp/eval-out --seed 42
```

- Collect artifacts for a triage ticket:
  1. Attach harness run folder (/tmp/eval-out) including raw outputs and scorer logs.
  2. Export top-100 failure examples as CSV.
  3. Tag triage issue with model-version and eval-run-id.

Reporting & Communication

- Weekly applied-ml QA sync: summarize notable regressions, open triage items, and quantization profile rollouts.
- Quarterly review: update prompt sets using production telemetry, retire stale prompts, and re-baseline core models.

Appendix: Example Eval Report Sections

1. Executive summary (1-2 paragraphs)
2. Key metrics & deltas vs baseline (table + charts)
3. Per-category failure analysis (top-5 clusters)
4. Human review summary (sample size, errors found)
5. Recommendations & next steps
